scope: Read-only timing suitability and counter-accounting review; no probe/product edits, no compilation, no Oracle access or workload execution
decision: No blocking counting or timing-accounting issue found in the finalized fixed plan/runner
probe_findings: hot15 black-boxes query input, the returned answer enum and the consumed packet length. Each declared iteration calls the real public local/cache answer path and changes/observes its real state; no timer, logging output or allocation-counter read occurs inside the loop.

Each query is primed and validates answer count, rcode and ID. Timed unexpected None or result variants still fail. The aggregate checksum is answer length, so it is a workload/coarse-regression sentinel, not full DNS byte equivalence.
The 800-name, 400-CNAME and 100-RRset populations all divide both fixed operation counts. Time passed to the answerer remains 101, so real elapsed time cannot expire the fixture mid-run.
Positive local/host, localisation, raw A/AAAA plus hosts, synthesis, leases, RRsets and cached/configured CNAME cover the important adverse paths for these two layout changes.

hit-typed still asks A/AAAA; hot15 has no dedicated ANY/PTR/MX/SRV/TXT timing scene. Existing functional gates remain the authority for those semantics; no fixture expansion is required for this limited screen.

The admission probe also black-boxes input and consumes every answer byte, with 800 warm iterations excluded from its allocation delta. It has different per-query validation/checksum overhead and is intentionally omitted from this nonduplicative timing plan.
runner_findings: Both PMU events must be user-only and inherited; perf verbose event-open records must show the same PID and a leader/member group_fd relationship.

The parser requires positive raw counts, one CSV/raw row per event, running==enabled>0 and 100 percent running. The final version also checks equal enabled/running values across events, so same-run user IPC does not mix independent windows or scaled values.

Each plain window launches a single taskset/nice/probe exec chain, waits for it, then differences RUSAGE_CHILDREN user+system CPU. No simultaneous child/build is running in this sequential runner, and perf wrappers exist only in stat windows.
All three native builds occur before measurement; source/probe hashes, per-window executable hashes, end-of-run hashes, fixed output checksums and zero instrumentation markers are checked.
PMU normalization uses the effective operations for that window, including the 200k stat windows and the two shorter plain controls.
The final operation counts and checksum constants were frozen before any layout measurement; all fifteen scenes and pair counts remain intact.
limitations: The probe header comment about setup/priming/output outside scope is true only for its allocation interval. The plan and runner correctly measure whole processes including those costs.
Plain CPU is the primary elapsed-cost measure. Recorded wall time also includes parent launch/wait/file handling latency and is not an isolated inner-loop timer.

Native repeated hot-loop measurements can keep code/data warmer than the low-rate whole-daemon owner workload. Planned separate exact-SDK owner windows are necessary; the native probe is not the shipping daemon ELF.
Host-localisation hash buckets depend on relocated pointer bytes. Keep every fixed pair and all adverse results; do not force seeds or selectively repeat.
Checksum equality does not prove record content/order/TTL equivalence or absence of every memory defect. The existing source reviews and Linux correctness gates supply that separate evidence.
minimum_changes_adopted: Predeclared known checksum table instead of first F sample setting the expected result.
Equal enabled/running time assertion across the grouped events.
